angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 685,265 km at 377.45 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.6493 +/- 0.0129 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 377.45 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.985 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Mancini et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.459.1393M/abstract): 685,265 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.081 +/- 0.034 solar masses from Mancini et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.459.1393M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5959 +/- 134 K from Mancini et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.459.1393M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mancini et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-36 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.459.1393M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-36.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.485, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WASP-36: main object type Em*, Emission-line Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-36 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.26 dex, from Mancini et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.459.1393M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-36 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.00087, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-36 (pscomppars): age 1.4 Gyr, from Mancini et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.459.1393M/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-36 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3.3 km/s, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
